name: Newel K. Whitney
dateNote: He was baptized in November 1830 and called as bishop in Ohio in December 1831; section 117 tells him to leave Kirtland in July 1838.
importance: Section 72 names him bishop in Ohio, alongside Edward Partridge in Missouri. His Kirtland store held the translating room and hosted the school of the prophets. Section 84 sends him to warn New York, Albany, and Boston, and section 93 tells him to set his family in order. Section 117 rebukes his “littleness of soul” and tells him to leave Kirtland.
connections: He married Elizabeth Ann Smith and had been the business partner of Sidney Gilbert. He served with Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon in the United Firm (78, 82, 104).

sources.title: Newel Kimball Whitney, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 3 or 5 Feb. 1795, Marlborough, Vermont; baptized Nov. 1830; bishop Dec. 1831; United Firm Apr. 1832; settled at Commerce/Nauvoo, not Adam-ondi-Ahman; “first bishop” Oct. 1844; died Sept. 1850, Salt Lake City. Bare “Newel” left out because it also names Newel Knight.
